headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because MinerU can ingest local documents while the RAG course agent reads/writes files and handles secrets.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP server, so attacker-controlled document text could be surfaced to the content-writing agent as instructions. The course agent reads files and uses stdin/stdout plus API endpoints, making a file-based bridge plausible. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into the course agent's prompt or notebook cells, injection becomes reachable.
IF the two agents share a workspace or MCP bridge, document text can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompting from extracted text.
Insert a manual review step before passing MinerU output onward.
Restrict the course agent to a separate workspace.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to extracted chunks.
requires-engineering: enforce instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU processes local PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX, while the course agent explicitly handles configuration secrets and writes files in a local development environment. If MinerU output or source documents contain secrets, the pair can move sensitive content into the writing agent's context and outputs. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF secret-bearing documents are processed by MinerU and then forwarded to the course agent, leakage is reachable.
IF both agents share a filesystem or notebook workspace, sensitive content can persist across runs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of documents fed to MinerU.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Rotate any exposed API keys after shared processing.
Redact outputs before handing them to the course agent.
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning before inter-agent transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is read-only on filesystem but uses APIs/MCP, while the course agent can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write files. They do not obviously contend on the same mutable resource by default, but if both are pointed at one workspace or notebook tree, the course agent can overwrite MinerU outputs. The overlap is plausible and not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, write conflicts become reachable.
IF the course agent runs notebook or shell steps against MinerU outputs, it can clobber files.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run one agent at a time on shared artifacts.
Make MinerU outputs read-only after generation.
Use git or filesystem snapshots before the course agent writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, OCR, and formulas that the content-writing agent could treat as authoritative inputs for RAG or agentic-ask flows. The course agent has downstream action-taking surfaces and can write files or invoke APIs, so a bad extraction can cascade into incorrect generated content or actions. No verification step is documented between them.
conditions: IF MinerU output is fed directly into the course agent's retrieval or writing pipeline, errors can propagate.
IF the course agent uses extracted facts without source verification, downstream mistakes become likely.
mitigations: Require source citation checks before writing.
Compare extracted facts against the original document.
Limit the course agent to drafting, not acting.
Flag low-confidence OCR for manual review.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency validation.

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private and fully offline, while the course agent runs in a local development environment but requests external API keys and handles secrets. If regulated or sensitive documents are processed, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches once the course agent sends data to third-party services. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency control, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated documents are sent from MinerU into the course agent's API-backed flows, residency risk is reachable.
IF the course agent logs prompts or outputs containing secrets, retention risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to API-backed steps.
Confirm retention settings for each external service.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive runs.
Purge local logs after each session.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency policy.
